## Implementation Analysis & Plan

Based on my exploration of the codebase, I can see that the threshold feature has been partially implemented across multiple layers. Here's a detailed implementation plan for completing this feature:

### Implementation Strategy

The threshold feature needs coordination across three main layers:

**Layer 1: CLI Argument Parsing (frai-cli/src/index.ts)**
- Parse threshold strings using regex pattern `<metric>=<number>`
- Validate format (metric ID is alphanumeric with underscores, value is 0-1)
- Handle multiple `--threshold` flags via Commander's variadic option
- Gracefully collect thresholds into array for validation

**Layer 2: Threshold Validation & Exit Code Control (frai-cli/src/index.ts)**
- Validate parsed thresholds against actual metric IDs from evaluations
- Exit code 2 for malformed input (invalid format or range)
- Exit code 2 for unknown metric IDs (with helpful listing of valid ones)
- Exit code 1 if any threshold check fails (report.passed === false)
- Exit code 0 if all thresholds pass or no thresholds specified

**Layer 3: Report Generation (frai-core/src/eval/index.js)**
- Accept optional `thresholds` parameter in `generateReport()`
- Compute threshold results: match metric ID, extract score, compare against min
- Treat null scores as failing their threshold
- Add `passed` (boolean) and `thresholds` (array) to report JSON
- Only include these fields if thresholds were actually evaluated

**Layer 4: Report Formatting (frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js)**
- Add "Thresholds" markdown section with PASS/FAIL indicators
- Show metric ID, min value, actual score, and status per threshold
- Use consistent formatting: `- **{metric}:** {PASS|FAIL} (min: {min}, score: {score})`
- Handle null scores as "n/a" in display

### Critical Data Flow

1. **CLI Input**: User provides `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.95`
2. **Parsing**: CLI parses into `{ exact_match: 0.8, toxicity: 0.95 }`
3. **Validation**: CLI checks these metrics exist in evaluations array
4. **Report Generation**: SDK generates thresholds array with pass/fail status
5. **Output**: JSON includes `passed` boolean; Markdown includes section
6. **Exit**: CLI exits with appropriate code based on `passed` status

### Custom Metrics Support

The implementation automatically supports custom metrics because:
- `runEvaluations()` accepts custom metric functions via the `metrics` parameter
- Each metric returns an object with an `id` field
- The CLI validates against whatever metric IDs are in the evaluations array
- SDK users can call `generateReport()` directly with custom metrics + thresholds

### Key Implementation Details

**Threshold Parsing Requirements:**
- Regex: `/^([a-z_]+)=([0-9.]+)$/` (metric IDs are lowercase with underscores)
- Range validation: `0 <= min <= 1`
- Error messages list all valid metric IDs on failure

**Report JSON Structure:**
```javascript
{
  metadata: { ... },
  metrics: [ ... ],
  passed: boolean,  // Only when thresholds evaluated
  thresholds: [     // Only when thresholds evaluated
    { metric: string, min: number, score: number|null, passed: boolean }
  ]
}
```

- Report generation with all thresholds passing
- Report generation with some thresholds failing
- Null score handling (should fail)
- Markdown formatting with thresholds
- CLI exit codes (0, 1, 2) validation

### Potential Implementation Challenges

1. **Multiple threshold flags**: Commander collects multiple options into an array; ensure handling matches both single and multiple occurrences
2. **Null score semantics**: Clearly document that `null` scores always fail (by design for safety)
3. **Metric ID validation**: Must happen after evaluations run but before report generation
4. **Exit code timing**: Exit with code 1 after writing the report (so CI/CD can see what failed)
5. **Backward compatibility**: Thresholds are optional; reports without thresholds should work as before

# FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) ## FRAI Ecosystem FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. | Project | What it does | Links | |---------|--------------|-------| | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | ### Short Answer - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. ### Why Keep Both? - Independent versioning and stability - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. - Reuse across surfaces - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. - Smaller, focused installs - Operators install the CLI. - Builders install only the core library they need. ### When to Use Each - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. ### Concrete Examples - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. --- ## Getting Started with the CLI 1. Install the published CLI: ```bash npm install -g frai ``` 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): ```bash frai --setup ``` Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 3. Run the interactive workflow: ```bash frai ``` FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. --- ## CLI Command Reference | Command | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | ### Default Command: `frai [options]` Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). - `--show-config` – display key storage status. - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. ### `frai generate [options]` Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. ### `frai scan` Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. # Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

# Threshold Feature Implementation Summary

## Overview
This document describes the implementation of the `--threshold` option for `frai eval`, which allows CI/CD pipelines to fail when evaluation metrics don't meet minimum requirements.

## Changes Made

### 1. frai-core Package (SDK)

#### packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
- Modified `generateReport()` to accept an optional `thresholds` parameter (object with metric IDs as keys and min scores as values)
- Added logic to compute threshold results for each metric:
  - Matches metric ID against evaluation results
  - Compares metric score against minimum threshold
  - Null scores automatically fail their threshold (safety default)
- Added `passed` (boolean) field indicating if all thresholds pass
- Added `thresholds` (array) field with per-metric threshold results: `{ metric, min, score, passed }`
- These fields only appear in the report when thresholds are actually evaluated (backward compatible)

#### packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js
- Enhanced `toMarkdown()` to include "Thresholds" section when thresholds are present
- Displays each threshold with metric ID, status (PASS/FAIL), minimum value, and actual score
- Format: `- **{metric}:** {PASS|FAIL} (min: {min}, score: {score})`

#### packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
- Added tests for:
  - Threshold application when all pass
  - Threshold application when any fail
  - Null score behavior (should fail)
  - Markdown report generation with thresholds section
  - Backward compatibility (no fields added without thresholds)

### 2. frai-cli Package (CLI)

#### packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts
- Added `threshold?: string[]` to `EvalOptions` interface
- Implemented `parseThresholds()` function to parse threshold strings:
  - Validates format: `<metric>=<number>`
  - Ensures metric ID contains only lowercase letters and underscores
  - Ensures minimum value is between 0 and 1
  - Throws descriptive errors for invalid input
- Implemented `getValidMetricIds()` helper to extract metric IDs from evaluations
- Modified `runEvalCommand()` to:
  - Parse and validate thresholds (exit code 2 for malformed input)
  - Validate that all threshold metrics exist in evaluations (exit code 2 for unknown metrics)
  - Pass validated thresholds to `generateReport()`
  - Exit with code 1 if any threshold fails
  - Exit with code 0 if all thresholds pass or no thresholds specified
- Added `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option to eval command
  - Can be specified multiple times
  - Documented in help text

### 3. Documentation

#### README.md
- Updated `frai eval` command documentation with threshold option
- Included description of behavior (exit codes, valid metrics, format)

#### docs/eval_harness_design.md
- Added "Threshold Feature" section documenting:
  - Syntax and usage
  - Exit code behavior
  - Integration with custom metrics
  - Safety semantics (null scores fail)

## Exit Code Behavior
- **Exit 0**: All thresholds pass, or no thresholds specified
- **Exit 1**: At least one threshold fails
- **Exit 2**: Malformed threshold (invalid format or range) or unknown metric ID

## Error Messages
When malformed input is detected, the CLI prints:
- Description of what's wrong (format, range, unknown metric)
- List of valid metric IDs available in the current evaluation

## SDK Usage Example
```javascript
const evaluations = Eval.runEvaluations({
  outputs: modelOutputs,
  references: goldReferences
});

const report = Eval.generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath: 'outputs.json',
  referencesPath: 'references.json',
  thresholds: {
    exact_match: 0.8,
    toxicity: 0.95
  }
});

// report.passed === false if any threshold fails
// report.thresholds contains details for each threshold
```

## CLI Usage Example
```bash
frai eval \
  --outputs model-outputs.json \
  --references gold-references.json \
  --threshold exact_match=0.8 \
  --threshold toxicity=0.95 \
  --report eval-report.json
```

## Backward Compatibility
- Without `--threshold` options, reports and exit codes work exactly as before
- `passed` and `thresholds` fields only appear in reports when thresholds are specified
- Existing code using the SDK without thresholds is unaffected

## Custom Metrics Support
The feature automatically works with custom metrics because:
- Metrics provided to `runEvaluations()` can be custom functions with their own IDs
- CLI validates thresholds against whatever metric IDs are in the evaluation results
- SDK users can call `generateReport()` with any combination of metrics and thresholds
